What your website says instead

Your website headline today

What it could say

“Three generations of East Valley garage doors. Since 1972.”

  • Your story isn’t told

    Your Thumbtack page says the business was founded in 1972 by your grandfather. Your website says “over five decades” and never tells the story.

  • Gilbert or Mesa?

    The headline says “Garage Door Company in Gilbert, AZ” while the copy targets Mesa and mentions Pinal County. Google can’t tell which city you’re for, and you don’t rank for either.

  • 544 reviews, not on the homepage

    Your Google rating is a perfect 5.0 from 544 reviews, more than most of Mesa’s top five. Visitors never see it.

  • Slow on phones

    Google’s speed test scores most of your pages 45–50 on mobile; the main image takes about 6 seconds to appear.

  • “$10% OFF”

    The coupon has a typo, and the menu repeats five times in the page content.

Google post

Since 1972, three generations of our family have kept East Valley garage doors running, and 544 neighbors have given us five stars on Google. Broken spring tonight? We answer 24/7, with no weekend or holiday upcharge. Call (480) 662-3315.

Facebook / Instagram caption

My grandfather opened JT's in 1972. Fifty-four years later, we're still the family you call when the door won't open. 🧡 Free estimates. 24/7. No holiday upcharge. (480) 662-3315 #MesaAZ #GilbertAZ #FamilyBusiness #GarageDoorRepair

Website article

What 54 years of garage doors taught us 1. Most emergencies start as a noise. A squeak or grind is a worn roller or a door out of balance; fix it early and it stays cheap. 2. Springs fail in cold mornings and hot afternoons. Arizona's temperature swings are hard on them. 3. Never pay extra for timing. A broken door on a Sunday is still just a broken door, so we don't charge weekend or holiday rates. 4. Always get options. A good tech shows you repair and replace, and lets you decide. Three generations in, those rules haven't changed. (480) 662-3315.
